prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, and for identifying cereblon as the target that explains molecular-glue degraders

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the only candidate on the shortlist that every member ranked, and it is the one where the supporting evidence is both mechanistic and cumulative. The PROTAC idea (Crews, Deshaies) recasts a small molecule as an inducer of proximity to a ubiquitin ligase, and the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target (Handa) supplies a molecular explanation for a long-unexplained drug action and, with it, the glue-degrader branch. Ternary-complex co-crystal structures now describe the mechanism in physical, atomic terms, which is the standard I apply. The three names map onto distinct, attributable steps (concept and first demonstration, target identification), so the three-person limit is workable without inventing a priority ranking. My own first choice, proton-coupled electron transfer (B004), was not ranked by any colleague, and a candidacy that rests on a line of work with unresolved priority among Meyer, Mayer and Nocera should not be pressed against a candidate with this breadth of support.
statement.case_against: No degrader has yet been approved, so clinical proof is still maturing, and the committee should ask whether the expert reports treat this as a completed discovery or an emerging modality. The credited list is long (Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray, Ito), and a Crews-Deshaies-Handa trio leaves out the VHL ligand and degrader-design work of Ciulli and the early Sakamoto-Crews-Deshaies PROTAC paper authorship, so the omission of credited contributors is a real fairness question. Handa's cereblon work and the PROTAC concept are also two lines of work, and a citation must hold them together without implying a single discovery.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B019) are the clearest case of molecular design that changed clinical practice, validated at pandemic scale and complementary to the 2023 Medicine prize; a Cullis, Madden, Anderson trio is defensible.
responses.response: I agree on the maturity and consequence, and I would keep B019 as a serious competitor, but I cannot yet see a defensible three-name attribution. Daniel, your trio omits Hope and MacLachlan from the Vancouver encapsulation work while Johan's trio omits Anderson, and our two colleagues who rank it first disagree with each other on who the three should be. The decisive step is also contested between formulation and lipid design. I would want the expert reports to settle that before supporting it over B056, where the credit divides along clearly different discoveries.

responses.point: Induced proximity to a ubiquitin ligase is a general catalytic chemical tool, and cereblon gives a chemical mechanism under thalidomide action; Andrei ranks it first and treats it as independently reproduced and timely despite the lack of an approved PROTAC.
responses.response: I largely share this and have moved toward it after reading your opening. Where I would qualify it is that the reproducibility is strongest for the molecular-glue and cereblon side, where imids are in routine clinical use, and less so for heterobifunctional degraders as a class. I would like the citation to be written so that it rests on mechanism, namely recruitment of a ligase and the cereblon target, rather than on the number of compounds in trials.

responses.point: Johan ranks the Car-Parrinello method first as an unambiguous two-name origin with four decades of validation, and ranks degradation third as a game-changer whose clinical proof is still maturing and whose credit among the PROTAC and glue branches is unsettled.
responses.response: We share the reservation on clinical maturity and on the long credit list, and I take your point that a trio is a compromise. I do not think the Car-Parrinello candidate is weaker on science; its attribution is cleaner than anything else on the list. My difficulty is that it is a method for computation, and I would not call it more in need of recognition than a mechanism-bearing biochemical modality. I would keep B058 in view, but I would not place it above B056 without a stronger argument that the field has been waiting for it.

responses.point: Nanopore sensing (B017) rests on a transparent physical principle, ionic-current blockade as a chemical readout, and became a long-read sequencing technology; Heiner ranks it first and ranks degradation only sixth.
responses.response: I agree the physics is transparent and the adoption is real, and I value that kind of principle. My reservation, Heiner, is attribution: the conceptual origin (Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer) is separate from the engineered pores and enzyme-controlled translocation that made it work (Bayley, Akeson), and the credited list contains five names with at least one apparently deceased. A three-person set will split the idea from the engineering, and I would want the reports to show which part carries the discovery before I rank it above B056.

responses.point: Xiaodong ranks halide perovskites first as a designed crystal architecture with new function, but also ranks degradation second as original, general and already consequential, with ternary-complex structures as confirmation.
responses.response: Your second-place ranking of B056 and your emphasis on co-crystal structures of ternary complexes is the argument I find most persuasive for maturity. On perovskites, I accept the reproducibility of the efficiencies, but with six credited names and unresolved stability and toxicity questions the three-person selection looks harder than for B056, and I would want to see how the experts weigh Miyasaka, Park, Snaith and Grätzel before treating it as ready.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports treat degradation as a completed discovery given that no PROTAC drug has yet been approved.
Whether the omission of Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito from a Crews-Deshaies-Handa trio is acceptable on priority grounds, or whether the prize should instead be framed narrowly.

Whether the proton-coupled electron transfer candidacy (B004) deserves discussion at all, given that I was alone in ranking it, and whether its priority question between Meyer, Mayer and Nocera can be resolved.
Whether nitrogenase (B052) will be regarded as premature while the catalytic mechanism remains unsettled.
statement.conflict_note: I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, and my own research is on respiratory-chain proton and electron transfer, which is adjacent to B004, B052 and Gray-type electron-transfer work; none of the shortlisted candidates is tied to Stockholm University or to me personally on the provided profile, so no specific recusal is apparent.
